uncited: The volume is conceptually permuted so the principal viewing axis aligns with the Z-axis, and slices are sheared to align viewing rays with the Z-axis (see [Shear-warp](24-shear-warp.md)).
This ensures volume sampling respects polygon occlusion.
**Warp:** Apply the 2D warp transformation $M_{warp2D}$ to the intermediate image to correct distortion and map to the final screen space (see [Shear-warp](24-shear-warp.md)).
**Final Composition:** Combine the warped volume image with the polygon data.
*   **Time Complexity:** Dominated by the Shear-warp volume rendering, which is generally $O(N)$ where $N$ is the number of volume samples, accelerated by RLE and early ray termination.
Polygon scan-conversion is $O(P)$ where $P$ is the number of polygons.
